source.title: A Seven-tone Dialect in Southern China with Falling-Rising-Falling Contour: A Linguistic Acoustic Analysis
source.rights: Copyright 2008 ISCA. No open reuse licence found; proposed bounded factual selection only, without scans, audio or substantial prose redistribution.

scope.speakers: Twelve middle-aged native speakers (six male, six female) recorded; three female speakers excluded from acoustic analysis, leaving nine. No exact town, recording date or ages stated.
scope.modernClassification: Xiang / Yong–Quan / Dong–Qi, independently supported by Wang Zhongli 2020 publisher abstract. This does not identify the 2008 speakers with Wang’s survey sites.

toneScope: Supplied numeric contours in Table 1, not T1–T7 tone class labels. Four targets 3243 and 2143 must remain intact. Do not substitute the six-tone Hu2011 or four-level MRFL Zhu2012 analysis.
phonationReview: Table prints diaeresis ABOVE p and BELOW a, t and i. Paper sections 4.1.1 and 4.1.3 describe these as slack-voiced obstruents. Published IPA preserves the exact above/below glyph positions. No p̈→p̤ normalization, p→b change or phonation deletion is performed. Unicode 17 chapter 7 Table 7-5 cautions that above and below diaeresis have distinct standard semantics; the source-specific description therefore stays beside the forms.

held.reason: Source gives only broad plant; not a well-defined everyday lexical meaning.
